question:
(a) Evaluate $\sec^{-1}\left(\sec\dfrac{5\pi}{3}\right)$ by identifying the correct principal value.

(b) Evaluate $\csc^{-1}\left(\csc\dfrac{7\pi}{6}\right)$ and justify why the original angle cannot be returned directly.
explanation:
(a)
The principal-value range of $\sec^{-1}x$ is
$$[0,\pi]-\left\{\frac{\pi}{2}\right\}$$
Now,
$$\sec\frac{5\pi}{3}=2$$
Therefore,
$$\sec^{-1}\left(\sec\frac{5\pi}{3}\right)=\sec^{-1}(2)$$
The angle in the principal range whose secant is $2$ is $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$. Hence,
$$\sec^{-1}\left(\sec\frac{5\pi}{3}\right)=\frac{\pi}{3}$$

(b)
The principal-value range of $\csc^{-1}x$ is
$$\left[-\frac{\pi}{2},0\right)\cup\left(0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right]$$
Since
$$\csc\frac{7\pi}{6}=-2$$
we obtain
$$\csc^{-1}\left(\csc\frac{7\pi}{6}\right)=\csc^{-1}(-2)$$
The angle in the principal range whose cosecant is $-2$ is $-\dfrac{\pi}{6}$. Therefore,
$$\csc^{-1}\left(\csc\frac{7\pi}{6}\right)=-\frac{\pi}{6}$$
The original angle $\dfrac{7\pi}{6}$ cannot be returned because it does not lie in the principal-value range of $\csc^{-1}$.
